newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P cuts Korea First Bank ratings to BBB-, A-3.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Korea First Bank ratings to BBB-, A-3.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Friday it had lowered its long-term debt and counterparty ratings of Korea First Bank to BBB- from BBB+ and its short-term debt and counterparty ratings for the bank to A-3 from A-2.
S&P added in a statement that it had removed all the bank's debt issues from Credit Watch where they were placed on January 19, 1997.
The outlook for KFB's long-term debt issues is negative, S&P said.
This rating action reflects the significant deterioration in KFB's asset quality that has occurred following the bankruptcies of two major customers, S&P said.
Exposure to one of the bankrupt companies, the Hanbo Group, roughly equals the value of the bank's conslidated equity, it said.
It said resolution of the two problem-loan situations would have a substantial impact on the bank's financial parameters even if rescue efforts limited the actual write-off amounts.

S&P said that in the restructuring process, the bank would most likely be required to make substantial interest-rate concessions that could have a negative effect on its profitability and ability to generate capital internally.

S&P added that it has been concerned about the Korean banking sector's large credit exposure to single or groups of borrowers as restructuring of the domestic economy increased the risk that asset quality may become more volatile in the medium term.
Korea First Bank, which also has a need to solve its asset-quality problems, may suffer more than other banks as it has had more exposure to the troubled heavy-industry sector, it said.

S&P said the bank's BBB category was retained due to its importance to the Korean banking system and the likelihood that the Seoul government would engineer the restructuring of Hanbo and support the bank if necessary.

The negative outlook reflected the chance that the bank may need to absorb a larger financial burden than currently expected and also the possibility that other asset-quality problems may arise as the industrial sector is revamped.
